materialChanges: Changed the clinical wrap-up to claims-mapped, mapped all three applicable claims to it, added its complete learner-visible source note, linked its glossary terms, and made every microbiology detail an explicit fictional mathematical input.

Added one NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions reference for power definitions, identities, and principal-value boundaries; replaced the unsupported exponent-law claim link to the notation-only NIST source and updated every affected scene source note.
Added a clinical self-explanation check with feedback that distinguishes multiplying repeated reduction factors from adding them.

reviewDispositions.rationale: The clinical wrap-up is now claims-mapped; claim-power-notation, claim-exponent-laws, and claim-magnitude-check all include scene-clinical-wrap-up; the scene exposes their complete source set; and its domain labels, model, and numbers are explicitly stipulated fictional inputs rather than microbiology assertions.

A versioned NIST DLMF reference with exact sections and equation locators now supports the broader power definitions, identities, and principal-value boundary. claim-exponent-laws cites that source as synthesis, the notation-only NIST source no longer supports that claim, and every scene naming the claim lists the DLMF source.
The worked model now declares the side count as a nonnegative integer and explicitly solves over the nonnegative reals before checking integrality.
The inverse-square answer remains correct on independent recomputation: 1/(2.4)^2 = 25/144, it lies strictly between 1/9 and 1/4, and the positive inverse factor for one-ninth is 3.
The clinical worked example now ends with a check that asks learners to explain the controlling exponent operation before feedback distinguishes multiplication of five tenfold factors from addition.
lesson.json now declares scene-clinical-wrap-up claims-mapped, and all three applicable claim records include that scene.
The clinical scene now contains a learner-visible source note naming all three mapped claims and their complete supporting set: the NIST notation, DLMF powers, and estimation records.
The frozen candidate identity, version 0.2.0, scene order, objectives, and file mappings were confirmed; the revised pack preserves identity, version, order, objectives, and status.

evidenceChecked: All eight scenes retain one level-one heading, logical source order, text-first explanations, and constrained Markdown directives; the revised pack contains no raw HTML, entities, Markdown images, remote embeds, executable content, or unsafe path references.

Every mathematical operation needed for the outcome appears as TeX plus nearby prose, reasoning, feedback, or interpretation; no distinction depends on superscript size, color, position, sound, motion, hover, dragging, or timing.
The added clinical check is a text response with its prompt before canonical feedback, so keyboard, nonvisual, reflow, print, and non-timed routes preserve the learning operation.
The assessment remains retakeable and untimed, uses text, numeric, or single-choice responses without pointer-only interaction, and every acceptableResponses entry is a JSON string.

All claims-mapped scenes expose every mapped claim and its complete supporting source set in same-scene source notes; all three references have allowed types, exact dates, HTTPS routes, use records, rights bases, rights evidence, and dated non-human-only agent-access records.

The added DLMF record is used only for factual support under an original-expression basis; its restrictive reproduction notice is recorded, no source expression or structure was copied, and no bulk copying was performed.

The lesson grant and attribution identify CC BY 4.0 original content, accountable authorship, material agent assistance, source use, and fictional settings. lesson.json declares no third-party assets, and the pack contains no dataset, image, audio, video, personal data, patient material, or real clinical measurement.
The clinical boundary states that every domain label, number, and model is fictional mathematical input, provides no care instruction, and makes no microbiology or clinical-practice assertion.
The finalizer run ID was absent from the candidate, author provenance, and both review artifacts before this adjudication; the two review artifacts remain byte-unchanged in the working tree.
limitations: The operator prohibited reads under site/ and prohibited npm, so the public adjudication/review schemas, graph and terminology ledgers, quorum-policy file, strict source preflight, and repository validator were not executed or independently inspected in this run; pack-local JSON, relationship, field, and arithmetic checks passed.

No rendered browser, screen reader, keyboard-only interface, 200% zoom/reflow, reduced-motion mode, print output, or planned non-web export was physically tested; the audit is of canonical static Markdown and JSON.
No real learner testing or microbiology protocol review was performed. The lesson avoids relying on either by limiting the clinical wrap-up to explicitly fictional arithmetic inputs.

Source-access and rights records are dated observations, not legal assurances. Agent providers, models, GitHub transports, and run isolation are disclosed and attested by the accountable operator rather than independently verified.
